subject: Staged private offer: pilot + annual term and approval path

Subject: Private offer question — pilot + annual renewal

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We liked the instance sizing and the routing options you showed. Two procurement questions as we map this into our SOW:

1) We'd prefer a staged purchase — a 3-month paid pilot (to validate latency and cost at our traffic) followed by an annual commitment if pilot metrics meet targets. Is it possible to structure a single AWS Marketplace private offer that captures both a short pilot term and an automatic annual conversion (or a manual opt-in) without forcing two separate purchase flows?

2) What buyer approvals do we need on our side for the pilot vs the annual? Procurement here has stricter governance for anything above $25k ARR.

Can you send a short sketch of what the private offer would look like (pricing buckets, activation windows, buyer approval gating) and any required artifacts for our procurement/legal? We want to get this into our procurement review early next week.

Appreciate it —
Priya
Procurement Lead | Stratus Analytics

Subject: Re: Private offer question — pilot + annual renewal

Hi Priya —

Great to meet you on the call. Short answer: yes, we can. Longer answer below with proposed structure and the approvals you'll likely need. See the attached one-page summary (stratus_priv_offer_summary.pdf).

Proposed structure (high level):
- Private offer with two line-items:
  1) Pilot SKU — 3-month prepaid term (fixed price) that includes a one-time onboarding credit and a capped token budget to validate latency/cost.
  2) Conversion SKU — 12-month commitment that is enabled once the pilot completes; this can be set up as a separate private offer activation step in AWS Marketplace to avoid automatically billing the annual until sign-off.
- Activation flow options:
  Option A (recommended): Pilot purchase first. At pilot completion, we provide a conversion quote and DocuSign for the annual. Buyer must approve/execute the annual to activate the conversion SKU.
  Option B: Single private offer with a conditional renewal clause — more complex on buyer-side procurement and may be flagged by finance.

Buyer approvals and gating (what Stratus should expect):
- Pilot: typical approvals for a one-off purchase; if below your internal $ threshold it can be treated as a procurement purchase order.
- Annual: procurement/legal signoff required (likely CFO or delegated approver for >$25k ARR).
- AWS Marketplace specifics: buyer needs an authorized AWS account user to accept private offers and to bind billing. We can provision the private offer to the exact buyer account ID once you confirm.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Please confirm expected pilot budget range (ballpark $) and the AWS account ID that will accept the private offer.
2) I'll loop in Vivek (finance) and Laura (legal/contracting) to scope the offer language and any special terms.
3) I attached a short summary and a sample SOW for the pilot.

If you want, we can build the private offer draft for you to attach to your procurement packet by early next week.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Private offer question — pilot + annual renewal

Karthik — quick internal notes on feasibility and approvals. Copying Ben to weigh in on pricing flex.

Feasibility notes:
- AWS Marketplace supports multiple line items in a single private offer. You can make the pilot non-recurring (one-time prepaid) and the annual a separate recurring SKU. The tricky part is the activation pattern — AWS does not provide a built-in "conditional auto-convert" after a pilot; conversion usually requires a new private offer or buyer acceptance of a subsequent change.

Recommended approach (least friction):
1) Create a private offer for the pilot (3-month prepaid).
2) Prepare a second private offer for the annual that references the pilot and includes a 30-day conversion window. Do not auto-bill; route conversion to a DocuSign then to AWS Marketplace activation.

Internal approvals required (we should scope for Stratus's procurement ask):
- Finance signoff: set the pilot discount ceiling and whether onboarding credits are allowed. (Vivek)
- Legal signoff: short SOW + contract language for conversion path and data handling during pilot. (Laura)
- Sales ops: ensure HubSpot deal has both SKUs and correct activation steps so activation is tracked. (Ben)

Pricing flexibility: Ben, suggest we offer up to 15% pilot discount and an onboarding credit of up to $5k. For the annual, standard tiered usage pricing with a committed spend band.

I can draft the private-offer wording for AWS (line-item descriptions, buyer acceptance instructions, activation window). Laura, once you sign off on a conversion clause that says "buyer must sign the annual DocuSign within 30 days of pilot end to activate the annual private offer," we can proceed.

Vivek
VP Revenue Ops | Redwood Inference
